items.title: Topic Twelve Opens: The Buddha's Own Wasted Toil, and the Path That Finally Worked

items.zh: 苾芻！苾芻！已度暴流耶？告言：如是，天！無攀無住，已度暴流耶？告言：如是，天！苾芻！汝今猶如何等無攀無住，已度暴流？
items.en: "Monk! Monk! Have you crossed the flood?" "I have, deity." "Grasping-free and lodging-free — have you crossed the flood?" "I have, deity." "Monk, in what manner now are you grasping-free and lodging-free, having crossed the flood?"

items.zh: 如如我劬勞，如是如是劣；如如我劣已，如是如是住；如如我住已，如是如是漂。天！我如如捨劬勞，如是如是無減劣。如是廣說鮮白品、此中祇焰頌應知。
items.en: Just as I once toiled, so did I decline; just as I declined, so did I stop; just as I stopped, so was I again swept adrift. Deity, just as I then relinquished that toil, so did I cease declining at all — the bright, pure path that follows is fully told in the verses of restatement that accompany this teaching.

items.zh: 今此頌中，無攀無住者，謂涅槃、滅定，如前已說。世尊依昔示現修習菩薩行時，所有最極難行苦行非方便攝勇猛精進；又依示現坐菩提座，非方便攝勇猛精進斷遍知故；說如是言：天！汝當知，我昔如如虛設劬勞，如是如是我便減劣；如如減劣，如是如是我便止住；如如止住，如是如是又被漂溺。與此相違，應知白品。此中顯示修苦行時，非方便攝勇猛精進，名曰劬勞。行邪方便，善法退失，名為減劣。既知退失諸善法已，息邪方便，說名止住。捨諸苦行，更求餘師，遂於嗢達洛迦、阿邏茶等邪所執處，隨順觀察，故名漂溺。復於後時坐菩提座，棄捨一切非方便攝勇猛精進，所有善法遂得增長。如如善法既增長已，如是如是於諸善法不生知足，不遑止住，於所修斷，展轉尋求勝上微妙。既由如是不知足故，遂不更求餘外道師。無師自然修三十七菩提分法，證得無上正等菩提，名大覺者。此中四義，捨劬勞等四句經文，如其次第配釋應知。云何復依涅槃無依無住以顯差別？謂不能度諸煩惱纏隨眠暴流，略由四因。何等為四？謂最初有依耽嗜尋。依耽嗜尋為依止故，便有懈怠。又由懈怠為依止故，住異生分。住異生分為依止故，順生死流貪愛勢力，令於五趣生死河中順流漂溺。與此相違四種因故，能度暴流，如應當知。云何復依想受滅定以顯差別？謂如有一，先已證得想受滅定，復住放逸，多住想受，而不多住諸想受滅。由此因緣，退失滅定。由退失故，還復止住下地生因。住彼因故，心便定趣彼所得果。與此相違，應知白品四句差別。

items.title: Topic Thirteen: The True Benefit of Going Alone Into the Wilderness

items.zh: 獨臻阿練若，靜慮、棄珍財；為別有方求，為窺窬封邑。何不與人交，而絕無徒侶？
items.en: Alone you reach the forest retreat, meditating, having cast aside every treasure — do you seek some other end, watching for a chance at a fief and a title? Why not mix with others — why cut yourself off from every companion?

items.zh: 得義、心寂靜，摧妙色魔軍。我獨處思惟，受最勝安樂；故不與人交，而絕無徒侶。
items.en: Having attained the benefit, the mind is at peace, and the demon army of beautiful form is overthrown. Alone I dwell in reflection, receiving the most excellent ease — that is why I do not mix with others, why I cut myself off from every companion.

items.zh: 此因天女所問伽他。言得義者，略有二種。一者、證得沙門果義，二者、證得聖神通義。由初得義，超越一切生死大苦；第二得義，證八解脫，寂靜思惟現法樂住。又初得義，降伏可愛妙色魔軍；第二得義，獨處思惟，受勝安樂。此中意辯聖神通義。所以者何？謂如有一，為欲成辦聖神通義，為令解脫清淨圓滿，依十遍處方便修行；由此因緣，令遍處定清淨圓滿，亦令解脫轉得清淨圓滿鮮白，亦能成辦聖神通義。彼既了知此成辦已，便自通達我義已辦，沙門果義亦得成就，是真沙門。於求財者深修厭毀；於諸城邑交遊等處，了知其初、了知過患、了知出離，亦能了知趣出離行。生彼因緣，說名為初。無常、眾苦、變壞法性，是名過患。欲貪調伏斷除超越，名為出離。聖八支道，名趣出離行。若有於彼不見其初，乃至不見趣出離行。由是因緣，於具珍財有情等處，不能厭毀，城邑交遊，周旋不絕，而謂彼為心得寂靜；於出居家證八解脫靜慮定者內心寂靜，反生誹謗。由是彼於內心寂靜，則不堪能善見、善知、善鑒、善達。若第一義內心寂靜與此相違，則能善見乃至善達。復次，今當略辨上所說義。謂薄伽梵於此略示，諸受欲者、樂雜住者，非第一義內心寂靜；若有證得八解脫定，離諸愛味，名第一義內心寂靜。當知是名此中略義。

blocks.text: Two verse dialogues. In the first, the Buddha speaks of his years of austerities; in the second, a goddess asks a forest monk why he lives alone. **Both explanations are untranslated**; the commentary summarises them.

A deity asks how the Buddha crossed the flood, grasping-free and lodging-free. He answers: "Just as I once toiled, so did I decline; just as I declined, so did I stop; just as I stopped, so was I again swept adrift." When he gave up that toil, he ceased declining.

items: **Four words, four stages.** "Toil" is the extreme austerity of the bodhisattva years: vigour not guided by right means. "Decline" is losing wholesome qualities through wrong method. "Stopping" is giving up the wrong method on seeing the loss. "Drifting" is then seeking other teachers, Udraka and Ārāḍa, and following their views.

**The reversal.** Seated beneath the bodhi tree, he gave up all such toil; wholesome qualities grew; he was never content with them and kept seeking what was higher, and without any teacher cultivated the thirty-seven factors and attained full awakening.

**Why beings fail to cross.** Four causes: thoughts dependent on indulgence; from them, laziness; from laziness, remaining an ordinary being; and so craving sweeps one down the river of the five destinies.
**Falling from cessation.** Someone who has attained cessation but then lives heedlessly, dwelling much in perception and feeling, loses it, and is again on course for rebirth in a lower state.

blocks.text: Master Cháng Bǎi's story of a brahmin nicknamed "Parrot" makes the point: with the wrong method, even diligence is drifting.

A goddess asks a monk meditating alone in the forest: are you waiting for an opening, hoping for a title? Why not mix with others? Master Cháng Bǎi: "peeping through the gap" is an idiom for waiting one's chance. The monk: "Having attained the benefit, my mind is at peace, and the demon army of beautiful form is overthrown. Alone I reflect and receive the most excellent ease."

"The benefit" is twofold: the fruit of the ascetic life, and noble psychic power, which is meant here: through the ten totalities and the eight liberations, one abides in present happiness. Master Cháng Bǎi: noble psychic power is uncontaminated, mixed with no craving or pride. Such a one knows the origin, danger, and escape from wealth and society. Those who do not know it think the busy life is peace and slander the solitary meditator's peace instead.

quiz.q: What sequence does the black verse describe for the Buddha's past austerities?
options: as I toiled, so I declined; having declined, I halted; having halted, I drifted
quiz.why: "Just as I once toiled, so did I decline; just as I declined, so did I stop; just as I stopped, so was I again swept adrift." Master Cháng Bǎi: the Buddha awoke to having lost wholesome qualities and strength, and stopped the wrong method.

quiz.q: How does Venerable Miào Jìng define "toil" here?
options: the vigorous effort of austerities not included among the means — not a means to the noble path
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: this shows that, during the austerities, vigorous effort not included among the means is called "toil" — it is not a means to the noble path.

quiz.q: The note names the brahmin whose father was reborn as the family dog "Māyūra." What does the lecture say?
options: the lecture, following the Parrot Sutra, names him 鸚鵡摩牢兜羅子 — "Parrot"; Māyūra means peacock, so the note errs
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: there was a lay brahmin named 鸚鵡摩牢兜羅子, "Parrot" for short. He tells the story to show that with the wrong method, even diligence is drifting. The note's Māyūra means peacock, not parrot.

quiz.q: How do the two masters explain 窺窬 in "watching for a chance at a fief"?
options: 窬 is a small hole by the door, peeping through it; a classical idiom for waiting for an opening to act
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: 窬 is a small hole beside a door; peeping through it means waiting for a gap or opportunity to act. Venerable Miào Jìng: this is a classical idiom meaning to wait for an opening and then move.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi say noble psychic power differs from non-Buddhist psychic power?
options: it is uncontaminated, accords with the noble ones, mixed with no affliction, accompanied by no craving, views, pride, or doubt
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: this is not non-Buddhist psychic power; it accords with the noble ones, is uncontaminated, mixed with no affliction, accompanied by no craving, views, pride, or doubt — this is noble psychic power. Venerable Miào Jìng: the ascetic's fruit does not necessarily bring psychic power; when both kinds of benefit are attained, that is liberation in both ways.

quiz.q: Why can the noble one "overthrow the demon army of beautiful form," per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: there is no beauty in the mountains
the noble one does not find beauty beautiful, penetrating it as impure, impermanent, suffering, empty, and without self
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the noble one does not experience beautiful form as beautiful, but penetrates it as impure, impermanent, suffering, empty, and without self — so the noble one can subdue the lovely demon army of beautiful form.
